audit: re-run the retained A5 probes against the hardened tree and adjudicate each finding CLOSED / PARTIALLY CLOSED / OPEN
verdict_statement: Every forgery the A5 probes demonstrated is now refused, and the refusals were re-derived by execution rather than read out of a commit message: 13 of 18 tracked rows are CLOSED, 3 are PARTIALLY CLOSED and 2 are OPEN and untouched. What the plan did NOT do is give authority an origin outside the process. AuthorityRegistry.mint_root accepts any issuer string an in-process caller types; this node minted a root declaring issuer='owner:Brian Espinosa' and authority_ref='docs/architecture/HUMAN_AUTHORITY_GATES.md', received a genuinely issued CapabilityToken for 'secrets/keys.txt', and the adapter ran. The two production paths mint their roots exactly that way. The plan raised the bar from 'construct a dataclass' to 'call the mint ceremony', which is a real and measurable improvement, and it is not the audited boundary acceptance criterion 4 asks for.

findings.title: ConstraintEnvelope.digest_value is format-checked but never recomputed, and AuthorityRegistry keys on it
findings.measurement_before: A5 probe 1 P1.9: two envelopes with contradictory authority both registered under one digest; the second overwrote the first and authorize(D1,'push','docs/x.md') returned a token.
findings.measurement_after: probes/reaudit_probe1.txt. P1.9b: mint_root(b) while b carries a's digest -> AuthorityDenied 'envelope digest does not seal its contents'. authorize(a's digest,'push','docs/x.md') -> 'action is not granted', i.e. still a's narrow authority. The verbatim P1.9 is also refused, but by the root-ceremony rule, which is why P1.9b exists.
findings.residual: The seal is a plain sha256 over the envelope document. It proves the envelope has not been edited; it says nothing about who wrote it.

findings.title: A fresh ROOT envelope can be minted in-process with any authority
findings.measurement_before: A5 probe 1 P1.5/P1.6: register(fresh_root) accepted, then authorize('push') returned a token.
findings.measurement_after: probes/reaudit_probe1.txt P1.5 -> AuthorityDenied 'root envelope requires an explicit mint ceremony'. P1.6 -> 'authority envelope is unavailable'. BUT probes/reaudit_probe2.txt P7.1: mint_root accepts any caller-supplied issuer string. This node minted a root declaring issuer='owner:Brian Espinosa' and authority_ref='docs/architecture/HUMAN_AUTHORITY_GATES.md', with allowed_actions ('write','push','deploy') over path scope ('secrets',), received a genuine CapabilityToken for 'secrets/keys.txt', and EffectGateway.execute RAN THE ADAPTER. adapter_calls=['adapter ran'].
findings.why_not_closed: The audit's own remediation text says a root 'must originate from an externally authenticated record rather than an in-process constructor'. mint_root records a provenance; it authenticates nothing. Both production paths mint their own root this way: local_execution.py:215 issuer='phase7:local:fixture-owner', mission_adapter.py:151 issuer=f'mission:{suffix}:fixture-owner'. The bar moved from 'construct a dataclass' to 'call one method with a string'.

what_this_does_not_establish: That authority originates outside the process. mint_root records an issuer string; it authenticates nobody. P7.1 minted a root in the owner's name and spent it to completion.

Any cryptographic property. There is no key that an attacker does not also hold, and no signature anywhere in this plan. The envelope seal, the grant digest, the intent seal, the bundle manifest and the ledger chain are all plain sha256 over their own contents. They detect edits. They do not attribute authorship. The one 'keyed' construct -- the CapabilityToken issuance witness -- uses a module-level key any in-process caller can read, measured at P7.3.
That an in-process caller cannot get authority. It can: mint its own root (P7.1), or read the issuance key (P7.3), or issue its own delivery grant while the ledger is unanchored (P2.1).
That the delivery grant boundary holds in a real run. It holds in the fixtures. No production path anchors the ledger.
That containment on Windows is robustly covered. It is covered by one test.
That the retained A3 and A4 evidence is sound. Both A3 bundles fail verification, and no A4 remote receipt cites the sealed plan digest.
That the repo-wide suite passes. This node ran nine modules; the orchestrator ran the repository-wide suite separately.
Anything about behaviour under a real remote. Every measurement here is in-process, with fake adapters and no network.
not_measurable_in_this_environment: Whether an owner-anchored grant ledger would hold in a real deployment: no deployment path exists to anchor it, so there is nothing to run.
Whether the reconciliation wedge (residual 3) occurs in practice: it needs a real interrupted remote effect, which needs a credential and a network, neither of which this node may use.
Whether the two retained A3 bundles ever verified: the five absent files, including ledger.sqlite3, are not recoverable from what is committed.
Cross-process or post-restart behaviour of the issuance key and the grant ledger: both are process-local by construction, so a single-process probe cannot exercise the boundary they lack.
GPG signature validity beyond git's own %G? report: no keyring is configured on this host, so 'N' means 'no signature recorded', which is the fact being reported.
